known_limitations: One existing technical family and en-US only. The request is bound to supplied canonical interpretations; the composition does not execute scientific analysis.
Original source components and admitted findings remain unchanged. Decorative resource appendices are separately inventoried and have no scientific interpretation.

The current physical-line policy inserts only LF into canonical JSON before HTML escaping. It bounds ASCII paragraph wrapping in the pinned layout; arbitrary scripts and visual glyph equivalence are not newly qualified.
Independent expected digests bind request, resources, derived HTML, IR and final native inspection. Hash equality does not authenticate source origin, rights, consent or upstream authority.
The existing 64-page/16-MiB and per-worker CPU/memory/wall/descriptor bounds stay unchanged. Larger work refuses; no editorial truncation is introduced.
The outer elapsed-time acceptance bound is not parent-work preemption or whole-job aggregate resource enforcement. Arbitrary descendant cleanup and host contention remain outside this qualification.

The original candidate API does not persist output. The separate opt-in storage API provides exact current private-file readback only, with independent request/resource/result/PDF expectations and no automatic retry or repair. Power-loss durability and reboot survival are not qualified.
Inputs and children are revalidated between stages; hostile same-owner concurrent mutate-and-restore remains outside the boundary. No retry, fallback, PDF rewrite or post-render padding is performed.
Final publication, PDF/UA certification, human accessibility review, frozen editorial/index/citation conformance and supported execution remain unestablished.

Storage retains the existing 16-MiB PDF and 324-KiB manifest ceilings. A claimed run is single-use; incomplete attempts are preserved and refused. Data and directory sync precede the receipt commit, and a postcommit refusal may require explicit exact recovery. No hard storage deadline is enforced.

Output digests are exposed only on complete success. If a failed or lost first response leaves no independently retained trusted output expectations, explicit recovery remains unverified; stored manifest hashes are not a replacement trust anchor.
